feature_summary: Implement tbx.NumToWords(n int) string, an integer-to-English-words speller for 0..9999, exposed to guest programs as a bespoke, repo-local stdlib extension. The pristine repo has no stdlib/core/tbx.go and no tbx package, so guest programs calling tbx.NumToWords fail on the baseline; the reference implementation makes them pass.

rules: 1..19 unique words; teens are NOT "ten" + units.
Tens 20..90 are twenty..ninety; non-zero units joined with a single hyphen: 42 -> "forty-two".
Hundreds: "<units> hundred" + space + remainder, NO "and": 105 -> "one hundred five".
Thousands: "<units> thousand" + space + remaining 0..999: 1234 -> "one thousand two hundred thirty-four".
Exact multiples of 100/1000 have no trailing remainder; single-space separators; only hyphen is tens-units; no leading/trailing space.

reference_approach: A small decomposition speller in stdlib/core/tbx.go (package core). Tables ones[0..19] (index 0 = "") and tens[0..9] (indices 0,1 = ""). A belowHundred helper renders 1..99: <20 -> ones[v]; else tens[v/10] with, if units!=0, "-"+ones[v%10]. NumToWords short-circuits the out-of-range and zero cases, then appends "<ones[n/1000]> thousand", "<ones[n/100]> hundred", and belowHundred(remainder) parts (only when their slot is non-zero) and joins with " ". The file registers the callable in init() via stdlib.Values["tbx"] = map[string]reflect.Value{"NumToWords": reflect.ValueOf(tbxNumToWords)}, the same registration pattern every other stdlib/core/*.go file uses. The harness blank-imports stdlib/core, so init() auto-registers; no other wiring (no comp/interp/vm edits) is required.
discovery_required: The agent is told only the guest-visible contract (name tbx.NumToWords, signature, spelling rules) and an example interpreted call. It must read the existing stdlib/core/*.go files to discover the stdlib.Values registration convention and that a new package core file with an init() is auto-picked-up. The prompt deliberately does not name stdlib/core/tbx.go or describe the registration mechanism.
miss_prone_edges: teens spelled wrong: 15 must be "fifteen", not "ten-five" or "tenty-five"; 11 -> "eleven"
tens-units hyphen vs space: 42 must be "forty-two" with a hyphen and no space
exact ten with no units: 20 -> "twenty" (no trailing word, no dangling hyphen)
hundreds with no "and": 105 -> "one hundred five" (a common bug emits "one hundred and five")
hundreds skip the tens slot when units-only: 105 keeps a single space, no empty token
exact hundred: 100 -> "one hundred" with no trailing remainder
exact thousand: 1000 -> "one thousand" with no trailing remainder
full composition: 1234 -> "one thousand two hundred thirty-four"
thousand + units only (no hundreds, no tens): 2003 -> "two thousand three"
upper bound with every component: 9999 -> "nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine"
irregular tens spelling: forty (not fourty), fifty/fifteen

baseline_vs_accepted.baseline: fail (no tbx package; every guest program calling tbx.NumToWords errors at Eval). Hidden pass_rate ~= 0.0, well under the 0.9 gate. Visible 'go run ./tests_visible' also fails.
baseline_vs_accepted.accepted: pass (all 14 hidden checks pass = 1.000; visible passes).
